chunks: Al-Nuḍr narrated from Durust, from one of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily Allah sent two angels to the people of a city in order to overturn it upon its inhabitants. When they arrived at the city, they found a man supplicating to Allah and beseeching Him. So one of them told the other, 'Do you see this supplicant?' He replied, 'I see him, but I will proceed to do as my Lord has commanded me.' The first said, 'But I will not do anything before returning to my Lord.' So he returned to Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and said, 'My Lord, I went to the city and found Your servant so-and-so supplicating to You and beseeching You.' He said, 'Proceed to what I have commanded you, for indeed that man’s face has never changed out of anger for My sake, ever.'

key_terms.غَضَبًا لِي: out of anger for My sake

ai.seo_question: What sign of sincerity did Allah point to regarding the man who was supplicating in the city?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the angel Jibril (or Mikail) delays the destruction of a city to investigate a man whose constant supplication seemed to shield the inhabitants. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the man’s sincerity was proven not by his prayers alone, but by the fact that his face never turned from anger for Allah’s sake, indicating that his devotion was free from *riya'* (showing off) and self-admiration. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on inner purity of intention as the true marker of authentic worship.
